```{r}
# =============================================================================
# HPAI EUROPE: FINAL PUBLICATION ANALYSIS
# =============================================================================
#
# Purpose:
#   Reproducible statistical analysis for the HPAI migration/outbreak study.
#
# Analysis unit for occurrence models:
#   NUTS3 region × ISO year × ISO week
#
# Host systems:
#   Wild birds
#   Captive poultry
#
# # Canonical publication datasets:
#
#   publication_output/data/analysis_occurrence_wild.rds
#   publication_output/data/analysis_occurrence_poultry.rds
#   publication_output/data/analysis_count_timing.rds
#   publication_output/data/analysis_count_intensity.rds
#   publication_output/data/analysis_first_detection.rds
#   publication_output/data/region_lookup.rds
#
# Historical development workspaces are not required to reproduce
# the final publication analysis.
#
#
#
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. USER SETTINGS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Root directory containing the publication repository/output folder
DATA_DIR <- "D:/data_processed"

# Publication repository/output directory
OUTPUT_DIR <- file.path(
  DATA_DIR,
  "publication_output"
)

# Canonical publication datasets
PUBLICATION_DATA_DIR <- file.path(
  OUTPUT_DIR,
  "data"
)

# Set TRUE only when models should be refitted.
REFIT_MODELS <- TRUE

# Computationally expensive analyses are disabled by default.
RUN_BOOTSTRAP <- FALSE
RUN_REPEATED_VALIDATION <- FALSE

BOOTSTRAP_ITERATIONS <- 2000

set.seed(2026)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. PACKAGES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

required_packages <- c(
  "dplyr",
  "tidyr",
  "ggplot2",
  "scales",
  "splines",
  "glmmTMB",
  "lme4",
  "survival",
  "broom",
  "broom.mixed",
  "performance",
  "emmeans",
  "patchwork"
)

missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(
    required_packages,
    requireNamespace,
    logical(1),
    quietly = TRUE
  )
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing required packages: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "),
    "\nInstall these packages before running the analysis."
  )
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
  library(splines)
  library(glmmTMB)
  library(lme4)
  library(survival)
  library(broom)
  library(broom.mixed)
  library(performance)
  library(emmeans)
  library(patchwork)
})


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. OUTPUT DIRECTORIES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

dir.create(
  OUTPUT_DIR,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

dir.create(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tables"),
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

dir.create(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "figures"),
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

dir.create(
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "models"),
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)


# Small helper for publication tables
write_table <- function(x, filename) {

  path <- file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "tables",
    paste0(filename, ".csv")
  )

  write.csv(
    as.data.frame(x),
    path,
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  message("Saved: ", path)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. LOAD CANONICAL PUBLICATION DATASETS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

required_data_files <- c(
  occurrence_wild =
    "analysis_occurrence_wild.rds",

  occurrence_poultry =
    "analysis_occurrence_poultry.rds",

  count_timing =
    "analysis_count_timing.rds",

  count_intensity =
    "analysis_count_intensity.rds",

  first_detection =
    "analysis_first_detection.rds",

  region_lookup =
    "region_lookup.rds"
)


data_paths <- file.path(
  PUBLICATION_DATA_DIR,
  required_data_files
)


missing_data_files <- data_paths[
  !file.exists(data_paths)
]


if (length(missing_data_files) > 0) {

  stop(
    "Missing canonical publication datasets:\n",
    paste(
      missing_data_files,
      collapse = "\n"
    )
  )
}


# Load occurrence datasets
dtm_wild <- readRDS(
  file.path(
    PUBLICATION_DATA_DIR,
    "analysis_occurrence_wild.rds"
  )
)

dtm_capt <- readRDS(
  file.path(
    PUBLICATION_DATA_DIR,
    "analysis_occurrence_poultry.rds"
  )
)

# Load count-model datasets
count_model_data_minus5 <- readRDS(

  )
)

intensity_model_data <- readRDS(
  file.path(

    "analysis_count_intensity.rds"
  )
)

# Archived first-detection dataset
first_detection_exported <- readRDS(
  file.path(
    PUBLICATION_DATA_DIR,
    "analysis_first_detection.rds"
  )
)

# Country-to-macro-region lookup
region_lookup <- readRDS(
  file.path(
    PUBLICATION_DATA_DIR,
    "region_lookup.rds"
  )
)

message("Canonical publication datasets loaded successfully.")

PUBLICATION_DATA_DIR <- "D:/data_processed/publication_output/data"

dtm_wild <- readRDS(

cat(

# Expected dimensions of publication datasets
stopifnot(
  nrow(dtm_wild) == 360756,
  nrow(dtm_capt) == 360756,

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. STANDARDISE VARIABLE TYPES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

prepare_occurrence_data <- function(data) {

  data %>%
    mutate(
      NUTS_ID = factor(NUTS_ID),

      country = factor(country),

      host_type = factor(
        host_type,
        levels = c("captive", "wild")
      ),

      season2 = factor(
        season2,
        levels = c("autumn", "spring")
      ),

      iso_year_f = factor(
        iso_year_f,
        levels = as.character(2015:2025)
      ),

      outbreak = as.integer(outbreak)
    )
}


dtm_wild <- prepare_occurrence_data(dtm_wild)
dtm_capt <- prepare_occurrence_data(dtm_capt)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. DATA-INTEGRITY CHECKS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("CANONICAL OCCURRENCE DATA CHECK\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


cat("Wild birds dimensions:\n")
print(dim(dtm_wild))

cat("\nPoultry dimensions:\n")

# These are the dimensions previously verified against the final analysis.
expected_n <- 360756

if (nrow(dtm_wild) != expected_n) {

if (nrow(dtm_capt) != expected_n) {

cat("\nWild bird outbreaks:\n")

cat("\nPoultry season distribution:\n")

cat("\nWild bird year distribution:\n")

cat("\nWeeks since migration onset by season:\n")

print(
  dtm_wild %>%
    group_by(season2) %>%
    summarise(
      min_wso = min(wso, na.rm = TRUE),

)


cat("\nOutbreaks by season — wild birds:\n")

print(
  dtm_wild %>%
    group_by(season2) %>%
    summarise(
      outbreaks = sum(outbreak),

)


cat("\nOutbreaks by season — poultry:\n")

print(
  dtm_capt %>%
    group_by(season2) %>%

      outbreaks = sum(outbreak),

      proportion = mean(outbreak),

# Final hard checks
stopifnot(
  all(dtm_wild$outbreak %in% c(0L, 1L)),
  all(dtm_capt$outbreak %in% c(0L, 1L)),
  identical(levels(dtm_wild$season2), c("autumn", "spring")),
  identical(levels(dtm_capt$season2), c("autumn", "spring"))
)


message("\nCanonical publication datasets loaded and validated successfully.")
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# 2. DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.1 Combine canonical host-specific datasets for descriptive summaries
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

weekly <- bind_rows(
  dtm_wild,
  dtm_capt
) %>%
  mutate(
    Host = factor(
      host_type,
      levels = c("captive", "wild"),
      labels = c("Poultry", "Wild birds")
    ),
    Season = factor(
      season2,
      levels = c("autumn", "spring"),
      labels = c("Autumn", "Spring")
    )
  )


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

cat("Combined weekly dataset:\n")
print(dim(weekly))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.2 Overall outbreak occurrence by host
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

descriptive_host <- weekly %>%
  group_by(Host) %>%
  summarise(
    observations = n(),
    outbreak_region_weeks = sum(outbreak, na.rm = TRUE),
    proportion = mean(outbreak, na.rm = TRUE),
    percent = 100 * proportion,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\nOutbreak occurrence by host:\n")
print(descriptive_host)

write_table(
  descriptive_host,
  "01_descriptive_outbreaks_by_host"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.3 Outbreak occurrence by host and season
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

descriptive_host_season <- weekly %>%
  group_by(Host, Season) %>%
  summarise(
    observations = n(),
    outbreak_region_weeks = sum(outbreak, na.rm = TRUE),
    proportion = mean(outbreak, na.rm = TRUE),
    percent = 100 * proportion,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\nOutbreak occurrence by host and season:\n")
print(descriptive_host_season)

write_table(
  descriptive_host_season,
  "02_descriptive_outbreaks_by_host_season"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.4 Outbreak occurrence by host and year
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

descriptive_host_year <- weekly %>%
  group_by(Host, iso_year) %>%
  summarise(
    observations = n(),
    outbreak_region_weeks = sum(outbreak, na.rm = TRUE),
    proportion = mean(outbreak, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Host, iso_year)

cat("\nOutbreak occurrence by host and year:\n")
print(descriptive_host_year, n = Inf)

write_table(
  descriptive_host_year,
  "03_descriptive_outbreaks_by_host_year"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.5 Weeks since migration onset represented in the data
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

descriptive_wso <- weekly %>%
  group_by(Host, Season) %>%
  summarise(
    min_wso = min(wso, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_wso = max(wso, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_wso = median(wso, na.rm = TRUE),
    observations = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\nWeeks since migration onset represented in dataset:\n")
print(descriptive_wso)

write_table(
  descriptive_wso,
  "04_descriptive_wso_range"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.6 Empirical timing of outbreak region-weeks
#
# IMPORTANT:
# These are descriptive outbreak-week distributions.
# They are NOT model-predicted peak timing and are NOT the lag-model estimates.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

empirical_timing <- weekly %>%
  filter(outbreak == 1) %>%
  group_by(Host, Season) %>%
  summarise(
    n_outbreak_region_weeks = n(),

    mean_wso = mean(wso, na.rm = TRUE),

    median_wso = median(wso, na.rm = TRUE),

    q25 = quantile(
      wso,
      probs = 0.25,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    ),

    q75 = quantile(
      wso,
      probs = 0.75,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    ),

    p05 = quantile(
      wso,
      probs = 0.05,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    ),

    p95 = quantile(
      wso,
      probs = 0.95,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\nEmpirical outbreak timing relative to migration onset:\n")
print(empirical_timing)

write_table(
  empirical_timing,
  "05_empirical_outbreak_timing"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

spatial_summary <- weekly %>%

occurrence_variables <- c(

message("\nStep 2 completed: descriptive statistics generated successfully.")
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# 3. OUTBREAK OCCURRENCE MODELS
# =============================================================================
#
# Mixed-effects logistic regression of weekly outbreak occurrence.
#
# Separate models are fitted for wild birds and poultry.
#
# Fixed effects:
#   - weeks since migration onset: natural cubic spline, df = 3
#   - standardized migration intensity
#   - season (reference = autumn)
#   - calendar year (reference = 2015)
#   - standardized distance to surface water
#   - standardized distance to poultry production
#
# Random effects:
#   - NUTS3 nested within country
#
# This specification reproduces the final occurrence-model coefficients
# reported in the manuscript.
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.1 Model formula
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

occurrence_formula <- outbreak ~
  ns(wso, df = 3) +
  mig_sc +
  season2 +
  iso_year_f +
  water_sc +
  poul_sc +
  (1 | country/NUTS_ID)


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("OUTBREAK OCCURRENCE MODELS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")

cat("Model formula:\n")
print(occurrence_formula)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.2 Fit final host-specific models
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

message("\nFitting wild-bird occurrence model...")

m_wild_final <- glmmTMB(
  formula = occurrence_formula,
  data = dtm_wild,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

message("Fitting poultry occurrence model...")

m_capt_final <- glmmTMB(
  formula = occurrence_formula,
  data = dtm_capt,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

message("Occurrence models fitted successfully.")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.3 Basic convergence checks
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

model_diagnostics <- tibble(
  host = c("Wild birds", "Poultry"),

  convergence_code = c(
    m_wild_final$fit$convergence,
    m_capt_final$fit$convergence
  ),

  positive_definite_hessian = c(
    m_wild_final$sdr$pdHess,
    m_capt_final$sdr$pdHess
  ),

  n = c(
    nobs(m_wild_final),
    nobs(m_capt_final)
  ),

  AIC = c(
    AIC(m_wild_final),
    AIC(m_capt_final)
  ),

  BIC = c(
    BIC(m_wild_final),
    BIC(m_capt_final)
  ),

  logLik = c(
    as.numeric(logLik(m_wild_final)),
    as.numeric(logLik(m_capt_final))
  )
)

cat("\nModel diagnostics:\n")
print(model_diagnostics)

write_table(
  model_diagnostics,
  "08_occurrence_model_diagnostics"
)


if (
  any(model_diagnostics$convergence_code != 0) ||
  any(!model_diagnostics$positive_definite_hessian)
) {
  warning(
    "At least one occurrence model has a convergence/Hessian problem."
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.4 Extract fixed-effect coefficients
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_occurrence_results <- function(model, host_label) {

  broom.mixed::tidy(
    model,
    effects = "fixed",
    component = "cond",
    conf.int = TRUE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Host = host_label,

      OR = exp(estimate),
      OR_low = exp(conf.low),
      OR_high = exp(conf.high)
    ) %>%
    select(
      Host,
      term,
      beta = estimate,
      SE = std.error,
      z = statistic,
      p = p.value,
      OR,
      OR_low,
      OR_high
    )
}


occurrence_results <- bind_rows(
  extract_occurrence_results(
    m_wild_final,
    "Wild birds"
  ),

  extract_occurrence_results(
    m_capt_final,
    "Poultry"
  )
)


cat("\nFixed-effect results:\n")
print(occurrence_results, n = Inf)

write_table(
  occurrence_results,
  "09_occurrence_model_fixed_effects"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.5 Key interpretable coefficients
#
# Spline basis coefficients themselves are not interpreted as ordinary ORs.
# Here we extract the directly interpretable covariates used in the manuscript.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

key_terms <- c(
  "mig_sc",
  "season2spring",
  "water_sc",
  "poul_sc"
)

occurrence_key_results <- occurrence_results %>%
  filter(term %in% key_terms) %>%
  mutate(
    variable = case_when(
      term == "mig_sc" ~
        "Migration intensity (per 1 SD)",

      term == "season2spring" ~
        "Spring vs autumn",

      term == "water_sc" ~
        "Distance to surface water (per 1 SD)",

      term == "poul_sc" ~
        "Distance to poultry production (per 1 SD)",

      TRUE ~ term
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    Host,
    variable,
    beta,
    SE,
    z,
    p,
    OR,
    OR_low,
    OR_high
  )


cat("\nKey occurrence-model estimates:\n")
print(occurrence_key_results, n = Inf)

write_table(
  occurrence_key_results,
  "10_occurrence_model_key_estimates"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.6 Random-effect variance components
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_random_effects <- function(model, host_label) {

  vc <- VarCorr(model)$cond

  # Extract variance and SD directly from each random-intercept matrix
  bind_rows(
    lapply(names(vc), function(group_name) {

      V <- vc[[group_name]]

      tibble(
        Host = host_label,
        group = group_name,
        variance = as.numeric(V[1, 1]),
        SD = as.numeric(attr(V, "stddev")[1])
      )
    })
  )
}


occurrence_random_effects <- bind_rows(
  extract_random_effects(
    m_wild_final,
    "Wild birds"
  ),
  extract_random_effects(
    m_capt_final,
    "Poultry"
  )
)


cat("\nRandom-effect variance components:\n")
print(occurrence_random_effects)

write_table(
  occurrence_random_effects,
  "11_occurrence_model_random_effects"
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.7 Reproducibility checks against established final coefficients
#
# These values were independently recovered from the canonical datasets.
# The tolerance is deliberately tight enough to catch accidental changes in
# model specification while allowing trivial floating-point differences.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

get_beta <- function(model, term) {

  coefs <- fixef(model)$cond

  unname(coefs[term])
}


reproducibility_check <- tibble(
  Host = c(
    "Wild birds",
    "Wild birds",
    "Wild birds",
    "Wild birds",
    "Poultry",
    "Poultry",
    "Poultry",
    "Poultry"
  ),

  term = c(
    "mig_sc",
    "season2spring",
    "water_sc",
    "poul_sc",
    "mig_sc",
    "season2spring",
    "water_sc",
    "poul_sc"
  ),

  expected_beta = c(
     0.23475,
    -0.13290,
    -0.06452,
    -0.01084,

     0.02371,
    -0.23179,
     0.13007,
    -0.17955
  ),

  reproduced_beta = c(
    get_beta(m_wild_final, "mig_sc"),
    get_beta(m_wild_final, "season2spring"),
    get_beta(m_wild_final, "water_sc"),
    get_beta(m_wild_final, "poul_sc"),

    get_beta(m_capt_final, "mig_sc"),
    get_beta(m_capt_final, "season2spring"),
    get_beta(m_capt_final, "water_sc"),
    get_beta(m_capt_final, "poul_sc")
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    absolute_difference =
      abs(reproduced_beta - expected_beta),

    matches =
      absolute_difference < 1e-4
  )


cat("\nReproducibility check:\n")
print(reproducibility_check, n = Inf)

write_table(
  reproducibility_check,
  "12_occurrence_model_reproducibility_check"
)


if (!all(reproducibility_check$matches)) {

  warning(
    paste0(
      "One or more occurrence-model coefficients differ from ",
      "the previously verified estimates. Inspect table 12 before ",
      "continuing."
    )
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.8 Save fitted models
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  m_wild_final,
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "models",
    "occurrence_model_wild_final.rds"
  )
)

saveRDS(
  m_capt_final,
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "models",
    "occurrence_model_poultry_final.rds"
  )
)


message("\nStep 3 completed: final occurrence GLMMs fitted and exported.")


```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# 4. SPATIAL HETEROGENEITY: ICC AND MEDIAN ODDS RATIO
# =============================================================================
#
# For logistic mixed-effects models, residual variance on the latent scale is
# approximated by pi^2 / 3.
#
# Random intercepts:
#   country
#   NUTS3 nested within country
#
# ICCs quantify the proportion of latent-scale variance attributable to the
# spatial hierarchy.
#
# MOR expresses random-effect heterogeneity on the odds-ratio scale.
# =============================================================================


cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("ICC AND MEDIAN ODDS RATIOS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.1 Helper function
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_spatial_metrics <- function(model, host_label) {

  vc <- VarCorr(model)$cond

  # Identify the two random-effect components
  nuts_group <- grep(
    "NUTS_ID",
    names(vc),
    value = TRUE
  )

  country_group <- grep(
    "^country$",
    names(vc),
    value = TRUE
  )

  if (
    length(nuts_group) != 1 ||
    length(country_group) != 1
  ) {
    stop(
      "Could not uniquely identify NUTS3 and country random effects for ",
      host_label
    )
  }


  # Random-intercept variances
  var_nuts <- as.numeric(
    vc[[nuts_group]][1, 1]
  )

  var_country <- as.numeric(
    vc[[country_group]][1, 1]
  )


  # Logistic latent residual variance
  var_residual <- pi^2 / 3

  total_variance <-
    var_country +
    var_nuts +
    var_residual


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # ICC
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  # Variance attributable specifically to country
  ICC_country <-
    var_country / total_variance

  # Additional variance attributable to NUTS3 within country
  ICC_NUTS3 <-
    var_nuts / total_variance

  # Total spatial clustering
  ICC_combined <-
    (var_country + var_nuts) /
    total_variance


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Proportion of spatial variance at each level
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  spatial_variance <-
    var_country + var_nuts

  spatial_share_country <-
    var_country / spatial_variance

  spatial_share_NUTS3 <-
    var_nuts / spatial_variance


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Median Odds Ratio
  #
  # MOR = exp[ sqrt(2 * variance) * Phi^-1(0.75) ]
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  MOR_country <- exp(
    sqrt(2 * var_country) *
      qnorm(0.75)
  )

  MOR_NUTS3 <- exp(
    sqrt(2 * var_nuts) *
      qnorm(0.75)
  )

  # Combined spatial variance, useful as an overall measure
  MOR_combined <- exp(
    sqrt(2 * spatial_variance) *
      qnorm(0.75)
  )


  tibble(
    Host = host_label,

    variance_country = var_country,
    variance_NUTS3 = var_nuts,
    latent_residual_variance = var_residual,
    total_latent_variance = total_variance,

    ICC_country = ICC_country,
    ICC_NUTS3 = ICC_NUTS3,
    ICC_combined = ICC_combined,

    spatial_share_country = spatial_share_country,
    spatial_share_NUTS3 = spatial_share_NUTS3,

    MOR_country = MOR_country,
    MOR_NUTS3 = MOR_NUTS3,
    MOR_combined = MOR_combined
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.2 Calculate metrics
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

spatial_metrics <- bind_rows(

  calculate_spatial_metrics(
    m_wild_final,
    "Wild birds"
  ),

  calculate_spatial_metrics(
    m_capt_final,
    "Poultry"
  )
)


cat("Spatial heterogeneity metrics:\n")
print(
  spatial_metrics,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


write_table(
  spatial_metrics,
  "13_occurrence_model_ICC_MOR"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.3 Reader-friendly percentage table
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

spatial_metrics_summary <- spatial_metrics %>%
  transmute(
    Host,

    country_variance =
      variance_country,

    NUTS3_variance =
      variance_NUTS3,

    country_ICC_percent =
      100 * ICC_country,

    NUTS3_ICC_percent =
      100 * ICC_NUTS3,

    combined_ICC_percent =
      100 * ICC_combined,

    percent_spatial_variance_country =
      100 * spatial_share_country,

    percent_spatial_variance_NUTS3 =
      100 * spatial_share_NUTS3,

    MOR_country,
    MOR_NUTS3,
    MOR_combined
  )


cat("\nPublication-scale spatial summary:\n")

print(
  spatial_metrics_summary,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


write_table(
  spatial_metrics_summary,
  "14_occurrence_spatial_heterogeneity_summary"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.4 Save exact values used for manuscript checking
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

manuscript_spatial_check <- spatial_metrics %>%
  transmute(
    Host,

    combined_ICC =
      round(ICC_combined, 3),

    NUTS3_share_of_spatial_variance =
      round(spatial_share_NUTS3, 3),

    country_MOR =
      round(MOR_country, 2),

    NUTS3_MOR =
      round(MOR_NUTS3, 2),

    combined_MOR =
      round(MOR_combined, 2)
  )


cat("\nValues for manuscript cross-check:\n")

print(
  manuscript_spatial_check,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


write_table(
  manuscript_spatial_check,
  "15_manuscript_spatial_check"
)


message(
  "\nStep 4 completed: ICC and MOR calculated successfully."
)
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# 5. OCCURRENCE-MODEL VALIDATION AND DISCRIMINATION
# =============================================================================
#
# Final host-specific occurrence GLMMs:
#   m_wild_final
#   m_capt_final
#
# Validation metrics:
#   - ROC-AUC
#   - Precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC)
#   - Brier score
#   - Calibration intercept
#   - Calibration slope
#   - Calibration by predicted-risk decile
#
# Population-level predictions are used (random effects excluded), providing
# assessment of discrimination/calibration from the fixed-effect component.
# =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("OCCURRENCE MODEL VALIDATION\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.1 Required packages
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

required_validation_packages <- c(
  "pROC",
  "PRROC"
)

missing_validation_packages <- required_validation_packages[
  !vapply(
    required_validation_packages,
    requireNamespace,
    logical(1),
    quietly = TRUE
  )
]

if (length(missing_validation_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install these packages before running Step 5: ",
    paste(missing_validation_packages, collapse = ", "),
    "\nRun:\ninstall.packages(c(",
    paste0('"', missing_validation_packages, '"', collapse = ", "),
    "))"
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.2 Generate population-level predictions
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_validation_data <- function(model, data, host_label) {

  p <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = data,
    type = "response",
    re.form = NA
  )

  tibble(
    Host = host_label,
    observed = as.integer(data$outbreak),
    predicted = as.numeric(p)
  ) %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(predicted),
      !is.na(observed)
    )
}


validation_wild <- make_validation_data(
  m_wild_final,
  dtm_wild,
  "Wild birds"
)

validation_capt <- make_validation_data(
  m_capt_final,
  dtm_capt,
  "Poultry"
)


cat("Validation observations:\n")

print(
  bind_rows(
    validation_wild %>%
      summarise(
        Host = first(Host),
        n = n(),
        events = sum(observed)
      ),

    validation_capt %>%
      summarise(
        Host = first(Host),
        n = n(),
        events = sum(observed)
      )
  )
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.3 ROC-AUC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_roc_auc <- function(d) {

  roc_object <- pROC::roc(
    response = d$observed,
    predictor = d$predicted,
    levels = c(0, 1),
    direction = "<",
    quiet = TRUE
  )

  ci <- pROC::ci.auc(
    roc_object,
    method = "delong"
  )

  tibble(
    ROC_AUC = as.numeric(
      pROC::auc(roc_object)
    ),
    ROC_AUC_lower = as.numeric(ci[1]),
    ROC_AUC_upper = as.numeric(ci[3])
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.4 Precision-recall AUC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_pr_auc <- function(d) {

  positive_scores <- d$predicted[
    d$observed == 1
  ]

  negative_scores <- d$predicted[
    d$observed == 0
  ]

  pr <- PRROC::pr.curve(
    scores.class0 = positive_scores,
    scores.class1 = negative_scores,
    curve = FALSE
  )

  tibble(
    PR_AUC = as.numeric(pr$auc.integral)
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.5 Brier score
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_brier <- function(d) {

  tibble(
    Brier_score = mean(
      (d$observed - d$predicted)^2
    ),
    prevalence = mean(d$observed),
    null_Brier = mean(
      (d$observed - mean(d$observed))^2
    )
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.6 Calibration intercept and slope
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Predictions are converted to the logit scale.
#
# Calibration intercept:
#   observed outcome ~ offset(predicted log odds)
#
# Ideal = 0.
#
# Calibration slope:
#   observed outcome ~ predicted log odds
#
# Ideal = 1.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_calibration <- function(d) {

  eps <- 1e-8

  d <- d %>%
    mutate(
      predicted_safe = pmin(
        pmax(predicted, eps),
        1 - eps
      ),

      lp = qlogis(predicted_safe)
    )


  # Calibration intercept
  fit_intercept <- glm(
    observed ~ 1 + offset(lp),
    data = d,
    family = binomial()
  )


  # Calibration slope
  fit_slope <- glm(
    observed ~ lp,
    data = d,
    family = binomial()
  )


  tibble(
    calibration_intercept =
      unname(coef(fit_intercept)[1]),

    calibration_slope =
      unname(coef(fit_slope)["lp"])
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.7 Calculate all validation metrics
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_validation_metrics <- function(d) {

  bind_cols(
    calculate_roc_auc(d),
    calculate_pr_auc(d),
    calculate_brier(d),
    calculate_calibration(d)
  )
}


validation_metrics <- bind_rows(

  calculate_validation_metrics(
    validation_wild
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Host = "Wild birds",
      .before = 1
    ),

  calculate_validation_metrics(
    validation_capt
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Host = "Poultry",
      .before = 1
    )
)


cat("\nValidation and discrimination metrics:\n")

print(
  validation_metrics,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


write_table(
  validation_metrics,
  "16_occurrence_model_validation_metrics"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.8 Calibration by predicted-risk decile
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_calibration_table <- function(d) {

  d %>%
    mutate(
      risk_decile = ntile(
        predicted,
        10
      )
    ) %>%
    group_by(
      Host,
      risk_decile
    ) %>%
    summarise(
      observations = n(),

      events = sum(observed),

      mean_predicted_probability =
        mean(predicted),

      observed_probability =
        mean(observed),

      .groups = "drop"
    )
}


calibration_table <- bind_rows(

  make_calibration_table(
    validation_wild
  ),

  make_calibration_table(
    validation_capt
  )
)


cat("\nCalibration by predicted-risk decile:\n")

print(
  calibration_table,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


write_table(
  calibration_table,
  "17_occurrence_model_calibration_deciles"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.9 Risk enrichment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Because outbreak occurrence is rare, this is useful alongside ROC-AUC:
# how concentrated are observed outbreaks in the highest predicted-risk
# observations?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_risk_enrichment <- function(d) {

  baseline <- mean(d$observed)

  d %>%
    mutate(
      risk_decile = ntile(
        predicted,
        10
      )
    ) %>%
    group_by(
      Host,
      risk_decile
    ) %>%
    summarise(
      observations = n(),
      events = sum(observed),
      observed_risk = mean(observed),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      baseline_risk = baseline,
      enrichment =
        observed_risk / baseline
    )
}


risk_enrichment <- bind_rows(

  calculate_risk_enrichment(
    validation_wild
  ),

  calculate_risk_enrichment(
    validation_capt
  )
)


cat("\nRisk enrichment by predicted-risk decile:\n")

print(
  risk_enrichment,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


write_table(
  risk_enrichment,
  "18_occurrence_model_risk_enrichment"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.10 Publication-ready calibration figure
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

calibration_plot_data <- calibration_table %>%
  mutate(
    Host = factor(
      Host,
      levels = c(
        "Wild birds",
        "Poultry"
      )
    )
  )


p_calibration <- ggplot(
  calibration_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = mean_predicted_probability,
    y = observed_probability
  )
) +

  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +

  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +

  geom_point(
    size = 2
  ) +

  facet_wrap(
    ~ Host,
    scales = "free"
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(
      accuracy = 0.1
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(
      accuracy = 0.1
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Mean predicted outbreak probability",
    y = "Observed outbreak proportion",
    title = "Calibration of outbreak occurrence models"
  ) +

  theme_classic(
    base_size = 11
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11.5
    ),

    strip.background =
      element_blank(),

    strip.text =
      element_text(face = "bold"),

    axis.title =
      element_text(face = "bold")
  )


print(p_calibration)


ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "figures",
    "occurrence_model_calibration.png"
  ),
  plot = p_calibration,
  width = 7,
  height = 3.8,
  dpi = 600
)


ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "figures",
    "occurrence_model_calibration.pdf"
  ),
  plot = p_calibration,
  width = 7,
  height = 3.8
)


message(
  "\nStep 5 completed: occurrence-model validation generated successfully."
)
```

```{r}
)

)

# Display last
print(Figure2_final)
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# STEP 7 — OUTBREAK COUNT MODELS
# =============================================================================
#
# Two complementary negative-binomial mixed-effects analyses:
#
# 1. Migration-relative timing model
#    Data: count_model_data_minus5
#    Window: -5 to +12 weeks relative to migration onset
#    Timing: natural cubic spline, df = 4
#
# 2. Migration-intensity model
#    Data: intensity_model_data
#    Migration intensity standardized to 1 SD
#
# Both models account for:
#    - country / NUTS3 spatial hierarchy
#    - repeated NUTS3-year observations
#
# =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("OUTBREAK COUNT MODELS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.1 Verify canonical count-model datasets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (!exists("count_model_data_minus5")) {
  stop(
    "count_model_data_minus5 was not found in the loaded analytical workspace."
  )
}

if (!exists("intensity_model_data")) {
  stop(
    "intensity_model_data was not found in the loaded analytical workspace."
  )
}


cat("Count timing dataset dimensions:\n")
print(dim(count_model_data_minus5))

cat("\nMigration-intensity dataset dimensions:\n")
print(dim(intensity_model_data))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.2 Verify required variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

timing_required <- c(
  "outbreak_n",
  "weeks_since_mig_onset",
  "season",
  "host_type",
  "year_c",
  "macro_region",
  "country_code",
  "NUTS_ID",
  "iso_year"
)

intensity_required <- c(
  "outbreak_n",
  "mig_intensity_sc",
  "season",
  "host_type",
  "year_c",
  "macro_region",
  "country_code",
  "NUTS_ID",
  "iso_year"
)


missing_timing <- setdiff(
  timing_required,
  names(count_model_data_minus5)
)

missing_intensity <- setdiff(
  intensity_required,
  names(intensity_model_data)
)


if (length(missing_timing) > 0) {
  stop(
    "count_model_data_minus5 is missing: ",
    paste(missing_timing, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

if (length(missing_intensity) > 0) {
  stop(
    "intensity_model_data is missing: ",
    paste(missing_intensity, collapse = ", ")
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.3 Set reference levels consistently
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Reference categories used in interpretation:
#   season: autumn
#   host: captive poultry
#   macro-region: Eastern
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

prepare_count_data <- function(d) {

  d %>%
    mutate(
      season = relevel(
        factor(season),
        ref = "autumn"
      ),

      host_type = relevel(
        factor(host_type),
        ref = "captive"
      ),

      macro_region = relevel(
        factor(macro_region),
        ref = "Eastern"
      ),

      country_code = factor(country_code),
      NUTS_ID = factor(NUTS_ID)
    )
}


count_model_data_minus5 <- prepare_count_data(
  count_model_data_minus5
)

intensity_model_data <- prepare_count_data(
  intensity_model_data
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.4 Check migration-relative analysis window
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

timing_range <- range(
  count_model_data_minus5$weeks_since_mig_onset,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

cat("\nMigration-relative timing window:\n")
print(timing_range)


stopifnot(
  timing_range[1] == -5,
  timing_range[2] == 12
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.5 Count model 1:
# Migration-relative timing
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

count_timing_formula <- outbreak_n ~
  ns(weeks_since_mig_onset, df = 4) * season * host_type +
  year_c * host_type +
  macro_region +
  (1 | country_code/NUTS_ID) +
  (1 | NUTS_ID:iso_year)


cat("\nTiming-model formula:\n")
print(count_timing_formula)

message("\nFitting migration-relative count model...")


m_time_df4_minus5_final <- glmmTMB(
  formula = count_timing_formula,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = count_model_data_minus5
)


message("Timing model fitted.")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.6 Count model 2:
# Migration intensity and change over calendar time
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

count_intensity_formula <- outbreak_n ~
  mig_intensity_sc * season * host_type +
  mig_intensity_sc * year_c * host_type +
  macro_region +
  (1 | country_code/NUTS_ID) +
  (1 | NUTS_ID:iso_year)


cat("\nIntensity-model formula:\n")
print(count_intensity_formula)

message("\nFitting migration-intensity count model...")


m_intensity_full_final <- glmmTMB(
  formula = count_intensity_formula,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  data = intensity_model_data
)


message("Migration-intensity model fitted.")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.7 Model diagnostics
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

count_model_diagnostics <- tibble(
  model = c(
    "Migration-relative timing",
    "Migration intensity"
  ),

  n = c(
    nobs(m_time_df4_minus5_final),
    nobs(m_intensity_full_final)
  ),

  convergence_code = c(
    m_time_df4_minus5_final$fit$convergence,
    m_intensity_full_final$fit$convergence
  ),

  positive_definite_hessian = c(
    m_time_df4_minus5_final$sdr$pdHess,
    m_intensity_full_final$sdr$pdHess
  ),

  AIC = c(
    AIC(m_time_df4_minus5_final),
    AIC(m_intensity_full_final)
  ),

  BIC = c(
    BIC(m_time_df4_minus5_final),
    BIC(m_intensity_full_final)
  ),

  logLik = c(
    as.numeric(logLik(m_time_df4_minus5_final)),
    as.numeric(logLik(m_intensity_full_final))
  )
)


cat("\nCount-model diagnostics:\n")

print(
  count_model_diagnostics,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


write_table(
  count_model_diagnostics,
  "21_count_model_diagnostics"
)


if (
  any(count_model_diagnostics$convergence_code != 0) ||
  any(!count_model_diagnostics$positive_definite_hessian)
) {
  warning(
    "At least one count model has a convergence/Hessian problem."
  )
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.8 Type III tests
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

intensity_type3 <- car::Anova(
  m_intensity_full_final,
  type = 3
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
  tibble::as_tibble()

cat("\nMigration-intensity model — CORRECT Type III tests:\n")

print(
  intensity_type3,
  n = Inf
)

write_table(
  intensity_type3,
  "23_count_intensity_type3_tests"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.9 Export fixed-effect coefficients
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_count_results <- function(model, model_label) {

  broom.mixed::tidy(
    model,
    effects = "fixed",
    component = "cond",
    conf.int = TRUE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      model = model_label,

      # Exponentiated coefficients are incidence rate ratios
      IRR = exp(estimate),
      IRR_low = exp(conf.low),
      IRR_high = exp(conf.high)
    ) %>%
    select(
      model,
      term,
      beta = estimate,
      SE = std.error,
      z = statistic,
      p = p.value,
      IRR,
      IRR_low,
      IRR_high
    )
}


count_timing_results <- extract_count_results(
  m_time_df4_minus5_final,
  "Migration-relative timing"
)


count_intensity_results <- extract_count_results(
  m_intensity_full_final,
  "Migration intensity"
)


cat("\nTiming-model coefficients:\n")
print(count_timing_results, n = Inf)

cat("\nIntensity-model coefficients:\n")
print(count_intensity_results, n = Inf)


write_table(
  count_timing_results,
  "24_count_timing_fixed_effects"
)

write_table(
  count_intensity_results,
  "25_count_intensity_fixed_effects"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.10 Random-effect components
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_count_random_effects <- function(model, model_label) {

  vc <- VarCorr(model)$cond

  bind_rows(
    lapply(
      names(vc),
      function(group_name) {

        V <- vc[[group_name]]

        tibble(
          model = model_label,
          group = group_name,
          variance = as.numeric(V[1, 1]),
          SD = as.numeric(
            attr(V, "stddev")[1]
          )
        )
      }
    )
  )
}


count_random_effects <- bind_rows(

  extract_count_random_effects(
    m_time_df4_minus5_final,
    "Migration-relative timing"
  ),

  extract_count_random_effects(
    m_intensity_full_final,
    "Migration intensity"
  )
)


cat("\nCount-model random effects:\n")
print(count_random_effects, n = Inf)


write_table(
  count_random_effects,
  "26_count_model_random_effects"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.11 Reproducibility fingerprint for intensity model
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# These coefficients were previously independently recovered from the final
# intensity analysis and provide a useful guard against accidental changes.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

get_count_beta <- function(model, term) {

  b <- fixef(model)$cond

  if (!term %in% names(b)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  unname(b[term])
}


intensity_repro_check <- tibble(
  term = c(
    "mig_intensity_sc",
    "mig_intensity_sc:year_c",
    "mig_intensity_sc:host_typewild",
    "mig_intensity_sc:host_typewild:year_c"
  ),

  expected_beta = c(
    0.202514249,
    0.019963041,
    0.014726904,
    0.005840984
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    reproduced_beta = vapply(
      term,
      function(x) {
        get_count_beta(
          m_intensity_full_final,
          x
        )
      },
      numeric(1)
    ),

    absolute_difference =
      abs(
        reproduced_beta -
          expected_beta
      ),

    matches =
      absolute_difference < 1e-4
  )


cat("\nMigration-intensity reproducibility check:\n")

print(
  intensity_repro_check,
  n = Inf
)


write_table(
  intensity_repro_check,
  "27_count_intensity_reproducibility_check"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7.12 Save canonical fitted models
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  m_time_df4_minus5_final,
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "models",
    "count_timing_df4_minus5_final.rds"
  )
)


saveRDS(
  m_intensity_full_final,
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "models",
    "count_migration_intensity_final.rds"
  )
)


message(
  "\nStep 7 completed: final outbreak-count models fitted and exported."
)
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# STEP 9 — LAG TO FIRST OUTBREAK
# =============================================================================
#
# Outcome:
#   Weeks from migration onset to the first outbreak detected in each
#   NUTS3 × year × season × host stratum.
#
# Models:
#   1. Basic: year × season
#   2. Regional: year × season × macro-region
#
# Separate models for wild birds and poultry.
# =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("LAG TO FIRST OUTBREAK\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9.1 Prepare weekly dataset
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

weekly_lag <- bind_rows(
  dtm_wild,
  dtm_capt
) %>%
  mutate(
    # Center year at 2020.
    # Centering does not change the estimated annual slopes.
    year_c = iso_year - 2020,

    season2 = factor(
      season2,
      levels = c("autumn", "spring")
    ),

    host_type = factor(
      host_type,
      levels = c("captive", "wild")
    )
  )


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9.2 First outbreak detection per NUTS3-year-season-host
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

first_detection <- weekly_lag %>%
  group_by(
    host_type,
    country,
    NUTS_ID,
    iso_year,
    season2
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    year_c = first(year_c),

    event = any(
      outbreak == 1
    ),

    lag_weeks = if (
      any(outbreak == 1)
    ) {
      min(
        wso[outbreak == 1],
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },

    mig_sc = mean(
      mig_sc,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    water_sc = first(
      water_sc
    ),

    poul_sc = first(
      poul_sc
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat("First-detection dataset:\n")

print(
  first_detection %>%
    summarise(
      strata = n(),
      outbreak_strata = sum(event),
      censored_strata = sum(!event)
    )
)


write_table(
  first_detection,
  "30_first_detection_data"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9.3 Keep event strata for lag models
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

lag_events <- first_detection %>%
  filter(
    event,
    is.finite(lag_weeks)
  )


cat("\nLag-model event observations by host and season:\n")

print(
  lag_events %>%
    count(
      host_type,
      season2
    )
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9.4 Add macro-region
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (!exists("region_lookup")) {
  stop(
    "region_lookup was not found in the analytical workspace."
  )
}


cat("\nregion_lookup variables:\n")
print(names(region_lookup))


lag_events <- lag_events %>%
  left_join(
    region_lookup,
    by = c(
      "country" = "country_code"
    )
  )


if (!"macro_region" %in% names(lag_events)) {
  stop(
    "macro_region was not created after joining region_lookup."
  )
}


if (any(is.na(lag_events$macro_region))) {

  warning(
    "Some lag observations have no macro-region assignment."
  )

}


lag_events <- lag_events %>%
  mutate(
    macro_region = factor(
      macro_region
    )
  )


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9.5 Model formulas
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

lag_basic_formula <-
  lag_weeks ~
  year_c * season2 +
  (1 | country/NUTS_ID)


lag_region_formula <-
  lag_weeks ~
  year_c * season2 * macro_region +
  (1 | country/NUTS_ID)


cat("\nBasic lag formula:\n")
print(lag_basic_formula)

cat("\nRegional lag formula:\n")
print(lag_region_formula)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9.6 Fit host-specific lag models
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

message("\nFitting wild-bird lag models...")

lag_wild_basic <- lmer(
  lag_basic_formula,
  data = filter(
    lag_events,
    host_type == "wild"
  ),
  REML = FALSE
)

lag_wild_region <- lmer(
  lag_region_formula,
  data = filter(
    lag_events,
    host_type == "wild"
  ),
  REML = FALSE
)


message("Fitting poultry lag models...")

lag_capt_basic <- lmer(
  lag_basic_formula,
  data = filter(
    lag_events,
    host_type == "captive"
  ),
  REML = FALSE
)

lag_capt_region <- lmer(
  lag_region_formula,
  data = filter(
    lag_events,
    host_type == "captive"
  ),
  REML = FALSE
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9.7 Export fixed effects
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_lag_results <- function(
    model,
    host_label,
    model_label
) {

  broom.mixed::tidy(
    model,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Host = host_label,
      model = model_label
    ) %>%
    select(
      Host,
      model,
      term,
      estimate,
      std.error,
      statistic,
      conf.low,
      conf.high
    )
}


lag_results <- bind_rows(

  extract_lag_results(
    lag_wild_basic,
    "Wild birds",
    "Basic"
  ),

  extract_lag_results(
    lag_capt_basic,
    "Poultry",
    "Basic"
  ),

  extract_lag_results(
    lag_wild_region,
    "Wild birds",
    "Regional"
  ),

  extract_lag_results(
    lag_capt_region,
    "Poultry",
    "Regional"
  )
)


cat("\nLag-model coefficients:\n")

print(
  lag_results,
  n = Inf
)


write_table(
  lag_results,
  "31_lag_model_coefficients"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9.8 Likelihood-ratio comparison:
# Does allowing trajectories to vary by region improve fit?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

wild_region_comparison <- anova(

extract_lmer_random <- function(
    model,
    host_label
) {

  vc <- as.data.frame(
    VarCorr(model)
  )

  vc %>%
    filter(
      is.na(var2)
    ) %>%
    transmute(
      Host = host_label,
      group = grp,
      variance = vcov,
      SD = sdcor
    )
}
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# STEP 10 — COX TIME-TO-FIRST-OUTBREAK MODELS
# =============================================================================
#
# Outcome:
#   Time from migration onset to first outbreak detection.
#
# Data structure:
#   Counting-process format with one row per NUTS3-week interval.
#
# Follow-up:
#   Begins at migration onset (wso >= 0).
#   Stops at first outbreak.
#   Strata without an outbreak remain censored.
#
# Separate Cox models are fitted for wild birds and poultry.
#
# Covariates:
#   - standardized migration intensity
#   - standardized distance to surface water
#   - standardized distance to poultry production
#   - season
#   - centered calendar year
#
# Robust SEs:
#   clustered by NUTS3.
# =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("COX TIME-TO-FIRST-OUTBREAK MODELS\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.1 Prepare canonical weekly survival dataset
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

weekly_cox <- bind_rows(
  dtm_wild,
  dtm_capt
) %>%
  mutate(
    year_c = iso_year - 2020,

    season2 = factor(
      season2,
      levels = c("autumn", "spring")
    ),

    host_type = factor(
      host_type,
      levels = c("captive", "wild")
    )
  )


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.2 Construct counting-process data
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cox_data <- weekly_cox %>%

  # Survival follow-up begins at migration onset
  filter(
    wso >= 0
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    host_type,
    country,
    NUTS_ID,
    iso_year,
    season2,
    wso
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    host_type,
    country,
    NUTS_ID,
    iso_year,
    season2
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    # Weekly event indicator
    event = as.integer(
      outbreak == 1
    ),

    # Number of events before the current week
    prior_events = lag(
      cumsum(event),
      default = 0
    ),

    # Counting-process interval
    tstart = wso,
    tstop = wso + 1
  ) %>%

  # Retain intervals only through the first event.
  # Event-free strata remain fully observed and censored.
  filter(
    prior_events == 0
  ) %>%

  ungroup()


cat("Cox dataset dimensions:\n")
print(dim(cox_data))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.3 Verify one first event maximum per stratum
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cox_stratum_check <- cox_data %>%
  group_by(
    host_type,
    country,
    NUTS_ID,
    iso_year,
    season2
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    events = sum(event),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


if (any(cox_stratum_check$events > 1)) {
  stop(
    "Cox construction error: at least one stratum contains >1 retained event."
  )
}


cat("\nCox strata by host:\n")

cox_strata_summary <- cox_stratum_check %>%
  group_by(
    host_type
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    strata = n(),
    event_strata = sum(events == 1),
    censored_strata = sum(events == 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(cox_strata_summary)

write_table(
  cox_strata_summary,
  "37_cox_strata_summary"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.4 Model formula
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cox_formula <- Surv(
  tstart,
  tstop,
  event
) ~
  mig_sc +
  water_sc +
  poul_sc +
  season2 +
  year_c +
  cluster(NUTS_ID)


cat("\nCox model formula:\n")
print(cox_formula)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.5 Fit host-specific Cox models
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

message("\nFitting wild-bird Cox model...")

cox_wild_final <- coxph(
  formula = cox_formula,
  data = filter(
    cox_data,
    host_type == "wild"
  ),
  ties = "efron",
  model = TRUE,
  x = TRUE,
  y = TRUE
)


message("Fitting poultry Cox model...")

cox_capt_final <- coxph(
  formula = cox_formula,
  data = filter(
    cox_data,
    host_type == "captive"
  ),
  ties = "efron",
  model = TRUE,
  x = TRUE,
  y = TRUE
)


message("Cox models fitted successfully.")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.6 Export hazard ratios
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_cox_results <- function(
    model,
    host_label
) {

  broom::tidy(
    model,
    conf.int = TRUE,
    exponentiate = TRUE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Host = host_label
    ) %>%
    select(
      Host,
      term,
      HR = estimate,
      SE = std.error,
      statistic,
      p = p.value,
      HR_low = conf.low,
      HR_high = conf.high
    )
}


cox_results <- bind_rows(

  extract_cox_results(
    cox_wild_final,
    "Wild birds"
  ),

  extract_cox_results(
    cox_capt_final,
    "Poultry"
  )
) %>%
  tibble::as_tibble()


cat("\nCox hazard ratios:\n")

print(
  cox_results,
  n = Inf
)


write_table(
  cox_results,
  "38_cox_hazard_ratios"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.7 Proportional hazards assumption
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

ph_wild <- cox.zph(
  cox_wild_final,
  transform = "km"
)

ph_capt <- cox.zph(
  cox_capt_final,
  transform = "km"
)


ph_wild_df <- as.data.frame(
  ph_wild$table
) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(
    "term"
  ) %>%
  tibble::as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    Host = "Wild birds"
  )


ph_capt_df <- as.data.frame(
  ph_capt$table
) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(
    "term"
  ) %>%
  tibble::as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    Host = "Poultry"
  )


ph_results <- bind_rows(
  ph_wild_df,
  ph_capt_df
)


cat("\nProportional-hazards tests:\n")

print(
  ph_results,
  n = Inf
)


write_table(
  ph_results,
  "39_cox_proportional_hazards_tests"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.8 Concordance
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cox_concordance <- tibble(
  Host = c(
    "Wild birds",
    "Poultry"
  ),

  concordance = c(
    summary(cox_wild_final)$concordance[1],
    summary(cox_capt_final)$concordance[1]
  ),

  SE = c(
    summary(cox_wild_final)$concordance[2],
    summary(cox_capt_final)$concordance[2]
  )
)


cat("\nCox concordance:\n")
print(cox_concordance)


write_table(
  cox_concordance,
  "40_cox_concordance"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.9 Reproducibility check for key migration-intensity HRs
#
# Manuscript results previously reported approximately:
#   Wild birds: HR ~ 1.11
#   Poultry:    HR ~ 1.13
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cox_key_results <- cox_results %>%
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "mig_sc",
      "water_sc",
      "poul_sc"
    )
  )


cat("\nKey Cox effects:\n")

print(
  cox_key_results,
  n = Inf
)


write_table(
  cox_key_results,
  "41_cox_key_effects"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.10 Save fitted models
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  list(
    wild = cox_wild_final,
    poultry = cox_capt_final
  ),
  file.path(
    OUTPUT_DIR,
    "models",
    "cox_models_final.rds"
  )
)


message(
  "\nStep 10 completed: Cox time-to-first-outbreak models fitted and exported."
)

```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# STEP 11 — SENSITIVITY AND ROBUSTNESS ANALYSES
# =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("SENSITIVITY AND ROBUSTNESS ANALYSES\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11.1 OCCURRENCE MODEL:
#      NATURAL SPLINE VS LINEAR TIME-SINCE-ONSET EFFECT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

occurrence_linear_formula <- outbreak ~
  wso +
  mig_sc +
  season2 +
  iso_year_f +
  water_sc +
  poul_sc +
  (1 | country/NUTS_ID)


message("Fitting linear occurrence sensitivity models...")


m_wild_linear <- glmmTMB(
  occurrence_linear_formula,
  data = dtm_wild,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)


m_capt_linear <- glmmTMB(
  occurrence_linear_formula,
  data = dtm_capt,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)


occurrence_spline_comparison <- tibble::tibble(
  Host = c(
    "Wild birds",
    "Poultry"
  ),

  AIC_linear = c(
    AIC(m_wild_linear),
    AIC(m_capt_linear)
  ),

  AIC_spline = c(
    AIC(m_wild_final),
    AIC(m_capt_final)
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_AIC =
      AIC_linear - AIC_spline,

    preferred =
      ifelse(
        delta_AIC > 0,
        "Spline",
        "Linear"
      )
  )


cat("\nOccurrence model: spline vs linear timing\n")

print(
  occurrence_spline_comparison
)


write_table(
  occurrence_spline_comparison,
  "43_occurrence_spline_vs_linear_AIC"
)


# Likelihood-ratio tests
#
# Linear and spline models are not always conveniently interpreted as strictly
# nested in terms of parameterization, so AIC is the principal comparison.
# The LRT is retained as a supplementary diagnostic.

wild_spline_LRT <- anova(
  m_wild_linear,
  m_wild_final
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("model") %>%
  tibble::as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    Host = "Wild birds"
  )


capt_spline_LRT <- anova(
  m_capt_linear,
  m_capt_final
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("model") %>%
  tibble::as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    Host = "Poultry"
  )


occurrence_spline_LRT <- bind_rows(
  wild_spline_LRT,
  capt_spline_LRT
)


cat("\nOccurrence spline comparison — likelihood ratio tests:\n")
print(occurrence_spline_LRT)


write_table(
  occurrence_spline_LRT,
  "44_occurrence_spline_vs_linear_LRT"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11.2 POULTRY OCCURRENCE:
#      SURFACE-WATER EFFECT WITHOUT POULTRY PROXIMITY
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# This addresses the sensitivity question raised during manuscript review:
# does the positive water-distance association reverse after removing poul_sc?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_capt_no_poultry_proximity <- glmmTMB(
  outbreak ~
    ns(wso, df = 3) +
    mig_sc +
    season2 +
    iso_year_f +
    water_sc +
    (1 | country/NUTS_ID),
  data = dtm_capt,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)


capt_no_poul_results <- broom.mixed::tidy(
  m_capt_no_poultry_proximity,
  effects = "fixed",
  component = "cond",
  conf.int = TRUE
) %>%
  filter(
    term == "water_sc"
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    model =
      "Poultry model excluding poultry proximity",

    beta = estimate,
    SE = std.error,
    p = p.value,

    OR = exp(estimate),
    OR_low = exp(conf.low),
    OR_high = exp(conf.high)
  )


cat("\nPoultry water-distance sensitivity model:\n")
print(capt_no_poul_results)


write_table(
  capt_no_poul_results,
  "45_poultry_water_sensitivity"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11.3 COUNT TIMING MODEL:
#      SPLINE DEGREES OF FREEDOM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Final model uses df = 4.
# Compare with equivalent df = 3 and df = 5 models.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

count_timing_formula_df3 <- outbreak_n ~
  ns(weeks_since_mig_onset, df = 3) * season * host_type +
  year_c * host_type +
  macro_region +
  (1 | country_code/NUTS_ID) +
  (1 | NUTS_ID:iso_year)


count_timing_formula_df5 <- outbreak_n ~
  ns(weeks_since_mig_onset, df = 5) * season * host_type +
  year_c * host_type +
  macro_region +
  (1 | country_code/NUTS_ID) +
  (1 | NUTS_ID:iso_year)


message("\nFitting df=3 count timing sensitivity model...")

m_time_df3_minus5_sens <- glmmTMB(
  count_timing_formula_df3,
  data = count_model_data_minus5,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log")
)


message("Fitting df=5 count timing sensitivity model...")

m_time_df5_minus5_sens <- glmmTMB(
  count_timing_formula_df5,
  data = count_model_data_minus5,
  family = nbinom2(link = "log")
)


timing_df_comparison <- tibble::tibble(
  spline_df = c(
    3,
    4,
    5
  ),

  AIC = c(
    AIC(m_time_df3_minus5_sens),
    AIC(m_time_df4_minus5_final),
    AIC(m_time_df5_minus5_sens)
  ),

  BIC = c(
    BIC(m_time_df3_minus5_sens),
    BIC(m_time_df4_minus5_final),
    BIC(m_time_df5_minus5_sens)
  ),

  logLik = c(
    as.numeric(logLik(m_time_df3_minus5_sens)),
    as.numeric(logLik(m_time_df4_minus5_final)),
    as.numeric(logLik(m_time_df5_minus5_sens))
  )
) %>%
  arrange(AIC) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_AIC =
      AIC - min(AIC)
  )


cat("\nCount timing model spline-df comparison:\n")
print(timing_df_comparison)


write_table(
  timing_df_comparison,
  "46_count_timing_spline_df_comparison"
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11.4 Convergence checks for sensitivity models
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

sensitivity_diagnostics <- tibble::tibble(
  model = c(
    "Wild occurrence linear",
    "Poultry occurrence linear",
    "Poultry occurrence without poultry proximity",
    "Count timing df=3",
    "Count timing df=5"
  ),

  convergence = c(
    m_wild_linear$fit$convergence,

  ),

  )
)


cat("\nSensitivity-model diagnostics:\n")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# STEP 12 — OUT-OF-SAMPLE SPATIAL VALIDATION
# Supplementary Section S4
# =============================================================================
#
# Validation was performed using repeated 80/20 spatial holdouts.
#
# Two validation designs were evaluated:
#
#   1. NUTS3 holdout:
#      20% of NUTS3 regions were randomly withheld. Models were fitted to
#      the remaining 80% and evaluated on the withheld regions.
#
#   2. Country holdout:
#      20% of countries were withheld entirely. Models were fitted to the
#      remaining countries and evaluated on the withheld countries.
#      Predictions for entirely unseen countries were generated at the
#      population level (random effects set to zero).
#
# Validation was performed separately for wild birds and poultry.
# Discrimination was quantified using ROC AUC.
#
# Reported results:
#
#                         NUTS3 holdout    Country holdout
#   Wild birds                 0.815            0.746
#   Poultry                    0.812            0.726
#
# NOTE:
# Repeated validation requires fitting many GLMMs and is therefore not
# executed automatically by this publication script. The complete code
# required to reproduce the validation is retained below.
# =============================================================================


RUN_REPEATED_VALIDATION <- FALSE


if (RUN_REPEATED_VALIDATION) {

  library(glmmTMB)
  library(splines)
  library(pROC)
  library(dplyr)

  set.seed(2026)

  N_REPEATS <- 10
  HOLDOUT_FRACTION <- 0.20


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Model specification
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  validation_formula <- outbreak ~
    ns(wso, df = 3) +
    mig_sc +
    season2 +
    iso_year_f +
    water_sc +
    poul_sc +
    (1 | country/NUTS_ID)


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AUC helper
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  get_auc <- function(observed, predicted) {

    roc_obj <- pROC::roc(
      observed,
      predicted,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      direction = "<",
      quiet = TRUE
    )

    as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_obj))
  }


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # One NUTS3 holdout
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  nuts3_holdout <- function(data, held_nuts) {

    train <- data[
      !data$NUTS_ID %in% held_nuts,
    ]

    test <- data[
      data$NUTS_ID %in% held_nuts,
    ]

    fit <- glmmTMB(
      validation_formula,
      data = train,
      family = binomial
    )

    pred <- predict(
      fit,
      newdata = test,
      type = "response",
      allow.new.levels = TRUE
    )

    get_auc(
      test$outbreak,
      pred
    )
  }


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # One country holdout
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  country_holdout <- function(data, held_countries) {

    train <- data[
      !data$country %in% held_countries,
    ]

    test <- data[
      data$country %in% held_countries,
    ]

    fit <- glmmTMB(
      validation_formula,
      data = train,
      family = binomial
    )

    # Population-level prediction because countries in the test set
    # were not represented during model fitting.
    pred <- predict(
      fit,
      newdata = test,
      type = "response",
      re.form = NA,
      allow.new.levels = TRUE
    )

    get_auc(
      test$outbreak,
      pred
    )
  }


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Repeated validation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  results <- vector(
    "list",
    N_REPEATS
  )

  all_nuts <- sort(
    unique(dtm_wild$NUTS_ID)
  )

  all_countries <- sort(
    unique(dtm_wild$country)
  )


  for (i in seq_len(N_REPEATS)) {

    # Same holdout units used for both hosts within each repetition.

    held_nuts <- sample(
      all_nuts,
      ceiling(
        HOLDOUT_FRACTION *
          length(all_nuts)
      )
    )

    held_countries <- sample(
      all_countries,
      ceiling(
        HOLDOUT_FRACTION *
          length(all_countries)
      )
    )


    results[[i]] <- tibble(
      repetition = i,

      wild_NUTS3 =
        nuts3_holdout(
          dtm_wild,
          held_nuts
        ),

      poultry_NUTS3 =
        nuts3_holdout(
          dtm_capt,
          held_nuts
        ),

      wild_country =
        country_holdout(
          dtm_wild,
          held_countries
        ),

      poultry_country =
        country_holdout(
          dtm_capt,
          held_countries
        )
    )
  }


  validation_results <- bind_rows(
    results
  )


  validation_summary <- validation_results %>%
    summarise(
      across(
        -repetition,
        list(
          mean = mean,
          SD = sd
        )
      )
    )


  print(validation_summary)

  write.csv(
    validation_results,
    file.path(
      OUTPUT_DIR,
      "tables",
      "48_repeated_spatial_validation.csv"
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  write.csv(
    validation_summary,
    file.path(
      OUTPUT_DIR,
      "tables",
      "49_repeated_spatial_validation_summary.csv"
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}


cat(
  "\nStep 12: repeated spatial validation documented; ",
  "not rerun by default.\n"
)
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# STEP 13 — FINAL PUBLICATION AUDIT AND REPRODUCIBILITY OUTPUT
# =============================================================================

cat("\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("FINAL PUBLICATION AUDIT\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 13.1 Principal occurrence-model estimates
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

get_publication_effect <- function(model, host, term, label) {

  x <- summary(model)$coefficients$cond

  beta <- x[term, "Estimate"]
  se   <- x[term, "Std. Error"]
  p    <- x[term, "Pr(>|z|)"]

  tibble(
    Host = host,
    Effect = label,
    beta = beta,
    SE = se,
    OR = exp(beta),
    OR_low = exp(beta - 1.96 * se),
    OR_high = exp(beta + 1.96 * se),
    p_value = p
  )
}


publication_occurrence <- bind_rows(

  get_publication_effect(
    m_wild_final,
    "Wild birds",
    "mig_sc",
    "Migration intensity"
  ),

  get_publication_effect(
    m_wild_final,
    "Wild birds",
    "season2spring",
    "Spring vs autumn"
  ),

  get_publication_effect(
    m_wild_final,
    "Wild birds",
    "water_sc",
    "Distance to surface water"
  ),

  get_publication_effect(
    m_wild_final,
    "Wild birds",
    "poul_sc",
    "Distance to poultry production"
  ),

  get_publication_effect(
    m_capt_final,
    "Poultry",
    "mig_sc",
    "Migration intensity"
  ),

  get_publication_effect(
    m_capt_final,
    "Poultry",
    "season2spring",
    "Spring vs autumn"
  ),

  get_publication_effect(
    m_capt_final,
    "Poultry",
    "water_sc",
    "Distance to surface water"
  ),

  get_publication_effect(
    m_capt_final,
    "Poultry",
    "poul_sc",
    "Distance to poultry production"
  )
)

)

# 13.3 Empirical migration-relative timing

publication_timing <- bind_rows(

  dtm_wild %>%
    filter(outbreak == 1) %>%
    group_by(season2) %>%
    summarise(
      Host = "Wild birds",
      n = n(),
      median_week = median(wso),
      q25 = quantile(wso, 0.25),
      q75 = quantile(wso, 0.75),
      .groups = "drop"
    ),

  dtm_capt %>%
    filter(outbreak == 1) %>%
    group_by(season2) %>%
    summarise(
      Host = "Poultry",

  select(

    n,

    q25,
    q75
```

```{r}
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
```
